tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Identify the largest disk that is not yet on its goal peg, first move any smaller disks that block it to other pegs, then move the largest disk to its goal, and recursively solve the remaining disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the current configuration has the largest remaining disk not on its target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a small disk onto the final target peg before the larger disk is placed, leading to a deadlock.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth (largest) disk directly, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous stack of disks that are already ordered correctly.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move two disks together in one step, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response must end with a syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier extracts the last parseable list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing the move list inside a sentence or adding extra characters after it, causing the parser to miss the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Replay each move mentally (or on paper) from the given initial state and check that after the last move the configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before submitting the final move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Ending the move list before all disks have been placed on the target peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer should consist solely of the move list; any surrounding commentary, headings, or formatting will be ignored or cause parsing errors.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including a heading like 'Solution:' before the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, confirm that the source peg’s top disk matches the disk being moved and that the target peg is empty or its top disk is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 from peg 0 while disk 1 is still on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you intend to move a larger disk onto a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto peg 2 where disk 1 is on top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto a peg if a larger disk will later need to be placed there, unless you plan to move the small disk away first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store the smallest disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 onto the final target peg and then trying to place disk 5 there without moving disk 1 away.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, first relocate all smaller disks that sit above it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before attempting to move a larger disk that is blocked.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disk 2 is on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Smallest-disk cyclic move strategy
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Repeatedly move the smallest disk to the next peg in a fixed cyclic order (e.g., 0→1→2→0) and then make the only other legal move; this ensures progress without deadlock.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to free a peg or shift the smallest disk without breaking the ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving the smallest disk arbitrarily, causing a loop where the same state repeats.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation before emitting any moves or forget to include the list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least one move and ensure the move list is present as the final output.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops early, cutting off the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the entire sequence before output, and if needed, break long sequences into multiple lines but keep the list syntactically complete.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of the current stack ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit mental (or written) representation of each peg's stack and only move the top disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not anticipate that a larger disk will later need that peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the largest‑first strategy and avoid placing small disks on the goal peg until all larger disks are already there.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets the size ordering rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, check that the target peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
